newsitem.title: DUBAI: Emirates, Airbus sign $2 billion deal for 16 planes.
newsitem.headline: Emirates, Airbus sign $2 billion deal for 16 planes.

text.p: The state-owned Emirates airline and the European consortium Airbus Industrie Monday signed a $2 billion deal for 16 new A330-200 aircraft, making the airline Airbus's biggest customer for the widebody jet.
Emirates has an option for another seven aircraft, its chairman Sheikhh Ahmed bin Saeed al-Maktoum told a news conference, where he and Airbus managing director Jean Pierson signed the deal.
Eleven-year-old Emirates is the first airline in the Middle East to order the A330-200 and is the largest customer for the new twin jet, Airbus said.
"Although today we have one of the world's youngest fleets, the new aircraft will gradually replace the present Airbuses from January 1999 until the year 2002," Sheikhh Ahmed said.
"The total cost of the 16 aircraft is estimated at $2 billion, including engines," he said, adding "It was a good deal for Emirates ... an excellent deal."
Pierson said Airbus has agreed to assist Emirates with the sale of the 16 A310 and A300-600s the airline already has.
Sheikhh Ahmed said Airbus won the deal against competition from Boeing Co.'s 767 model.
He said Emirates had not yet decided on the engines, but added: "It is going to be between (Britain's) Rolls Royce Plc and General Electric Co." of the United States.
Asked how Emirates would finance the new planes, he said: "As usual. We never have any problem financing aircraft."
Emirates has in the past raised funds through local and international banks for aircraft purchases.
It recently took delivery of its third Boeing 777. It has another four 777s on order and an option for seven more.
